parts:
Hello,

I am trying to use plyr to apply a glm regression on a data set split
by region, but i am always getting this error.

The code i am using is :
<script src="https://gist.github.com/958618.js"> </script>

B_PA_KEPT_RATE contains NA cells and i know this is the cause of the
error but i don't know how to fix it. I tried to use failwith function
but i still don't seem do get it to work.

Is there a way to get past this error?

Thank you very much in advance,
Best regards,
Alex

The data i am using is (i hope it doesn't ruin the message):
<script src="https://gist.github.com/958625.js"> </script>

When I am outside plyr, and need to exclude variables that are

messages.subject: Re: dlply ERROR: 2, .Dimnames = list( when using GLM
parts:
Seems like the links without the .js are more helpful:

https://gist.github.com/958618
https://gist.github.com/958625

The error I get is:
Error in glm.fit(x = c(270.89, 0), y = 0, weights = NULL, start = NULL, :
subscript out of bounds

It's not clear this is the same error as you?

One way forward it is to "try" to fit your model and then get the
coefficients for the ones that fit without error:

tmp <- dlply(Dataset, "REGIUNE", function(df) try(glm(PYM ~0 +
MAIN_DEBT + B_PA_KEPT_RATE , family=binomial(logit), data = df)))
ldply(tmp[sapply(tmp, class) != "try-error"], coef)

Does that help?

Charlotte

the call into two steps and check.

MAIN_DEBT + B_PA_KEPT_RATE , family=binomial(logit), data = df)))

The warnings are just being discarded and should really be
investigated. I don't know of an equivalent of try or failwith to
capture warnings but it might be out there.
